pass1.sentence: Below 3 mg/mmol is normal to mildly raised (category A1); 3 to 30 is moderately raised (A2); above 30 is severely raised (A3).
pass1.note: NICE table: A1 <3 normal to mildly increased; A2 3-30 moderately increased; A3 >30 severely increased. 'formerly microalbuminuria' removed: not retrieved.

pass1.sentence: above 300 mg/mmol is called the nephrotic range in some NHS laboratory guidance
pass1.note: North Bristol NHS Trust: PCR >300 mg/mmol nephrotic range proteinuria; UHB/other trusts agree; Oxford says >350. This is a protein:creatinine ratio.

pass1.sentence: Staging chronic kidney disease and informing decisions on kidney-protecting medicines
pass1.note: Specific ACE inhibitor/SGLT2 inhibitor wording and ACR cut-off not confirmed (KDIGO 2024 excerpt cut off), so made general.

pass1.sentence: in the UK an ACR of 3 to 70 mg/mmol is usually confirmed with a repeat early-morning sample,
pass1.note: UK Kidney Association quick reference: ACR 3-70 repeat on first morning urine; 70+ no repeat.

pass1.sentence: and chronic kidney disease is diagnosed only when the abnormality lasts for more than three months.
pass1.note: kidney.org: CKD requires abnormalities present more than 3 months.
NICE: regard a confirmed ACR of 3 mg/mmol or more as clinically important proteinuria (existing sentence, kept with record).
